messages:
Carmen: FYI, saw a ~3% invoice bump after enabling model-compat-tokenizer on canary.
Carmen: It's specific to 2 routes that use dynamic batching + quantized models.
Ryan: hmm, can you paste an example event? link to dataplane trace?
Carmen: here's a sample event we sent to metering: ```json
{"request_id":"req_9a8f","model":"redwood-quant-v1","input_bytes":1024,"runtime_tokens":256,"metering_tokens":245,"route":"/v1/generate"}
```
Sophia: meter shows 245, runtime shows 256. Where are the missing 11 tokens coming from?
Dan: is this the same tokenizer change we rolled in q2? That swapped to unicode-grapheme pre-tokenization.
Carmen: yes, rolled in yesterday to reduce memory. runtime_kv cache counts align with runtime_tokens though.
Ryan: meters still rely on byte->token heuristic in ingest; not using runtime tokenizer result. That could explain a skew.
Sophia: but why only for quantized models + dynamic batching?
Carmen: guess: dynamic batching merges inputs and we run the tokenizer once on merged buffer -> dedupes some whitespace tokens. ingest path tokenizes per-request (pre-merge) so extra tokens.
Dan: ok we need to fix either metering ingestion or runtime to export final token_count in event. I'd prefer runtime export.
Ryan: +1 runtime export is authoritative but it's a bigger surface: change event schema and rollout of metering consumers.
Sophia: proposal: add optional field `final_token_count` to billing event. Backwards compatible if missing.
Carmen: minimal change. example schema delta: ```json
{"final_token_count":256}
```
Dan: also add a `tokenization_signature` header so we can reconcile historical diffs in queries.
Ryan: can we avoid a full dataset re-ingest? we can implement reconciliation in invoices by preferring final_token_count when present and falling back otherwise.
metering-bot: alert triggered: invoice_preview_diff > 1% for tenant T-324. link: https://console.redwood/alerts/324
Sophia: console UX note: preview mode currently shows only ingest_tokens. We should surface both ingest vs final and the reconciliation logic.
Carmen: agree — add a per-tenant toggle in Preview: show "Resolved token count" and the breakdown.
Dan: rollout plan: 1) runtime emits final_token_count + signature; 2) ingest pipeline tags events and writes both values to tallies; 3) console shows both and flags tenants with >0.5% delta; 4) schedule backfill if needed.
Ryan: implementation detail: ingest change is trivial; big work is consumers (billing-aggregator, quota-enforcer, invoice-preview). We'll feature-flag consumers.
Sophia: how about sampling rate for telemetry traces? We need traces for events that have deltas. Suggest we sample 100% for tenants where preview_diff > 0.2%, else 0.1%.
Dan: +1. add `reconciled=true/false` in event metadata for easier queries.
Carmen: test plan: canary to dedicated cluster with 5 tenants, run for 48h and compare invoice_preview deltas.
Ryan: I'll make a PR for the runtime export: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/452 (WIP)
Carmen: tagging @ryan @sophia when PR is ready for review.
ops-bot: deploy queued: metering-ingest v2 -> canary (id: deploy_778) by @ryan
Ryan: starting ingest change now, will keep feature flag off until runtime PR merged.
Sophia: UI issue: preview page will need to show the reconciliation rule (tooltip) and time-series of ingest vs final.
Dan: UX mock by EOD? @design please
Carmen: thx all. I'll start a short runbook for oncall steps if reconciliation causes negative invoices.
Ryan: noted. I'll add unit tests for both fields and cross-check in nightly job.
Sophia: also add a quick SQL snippet for ops: ```sql
SELECT tenant, SUM(final_token_count) - SUM(metering_tokens) as diff FROM billing_events WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY abs(diff) DESC LIMIT 10;
```
Carmen: perfect. closing loop after canary results.
